The part of a tree that grows underground is the **roots**.

Regarding the time period of the text, the clues point to the **Victorian era**, specifically the **mid-to-late 19th century** (roughly 1837–1901).

Here is the breakdown of the historical and contextual clues:

1.  **Gas Lighting and Horse-Drawn Carriages:** These were the dominant forms of urban infrastructure and transportation in major cities during the 19th century, before the widespread adoption of electricity and internal combustion engines.
2.  **Georgian and Victorian Architecture:** The mention of these styles places the setting in Britain or its colonies during the 18th and 19th centuries. The coexistence suggests a period where older Georgian buildings were still present alongside newer Victorian constructions.
3.  **Charles Dickens:** Charles Dickens was a prolific author whose works were published between the 1830s and 1870s. The fact that his works are "the talk of the town" indicates the text is set during his lifetime or shortly after his peak popularity, firmly placing the context in the mid-to-late 19th century.
